newsitem.title: USA: Baxter sees Q1 sales lower than expected.
newsitem.headline: Baxter sees Q1 sales lower than expected.

text.p: Baxter International Inc said on Monday it expects first-quarter sales growth to be in the low double digits, lower than expected.

It said this is due partly to inclusion of only two months of Immuno International AG's results. Baxter, which holds 99.3 percent of the share capital and 99.7 percent of the voting rights of Immuno, said it expects to complete the acquisition of Immuno by June 30.
However, chief financial officer Harry Jansen Kraemer Jr said he backed analysts' earnings outlook for Baxter's first quarter and full year.
"We are comfortable with Baxter's earnings outlook for both the first quarter as well as for the full year," Kraemer said in a statement.

The First Call consensus is for $0.55 per share for the quarter, compared to 1996's first-quarter earnings from continuing operations of $0.51 per share. For the full year, the consensus is $2.37; in 1996, Baxter posted earnings from continuing operations of $2.11.
"For the full year, we expect to generate sales growth in the 20 percent range including acquisitions, and net income in the low double digits," Kraemer added.
Baxter said in the first quarter of 1997 it also experienced lower-than-expected sales in its biotech business as a result of technical difficulties in producing certain products at its Hyland unit.
Baxter said it completed the $236 million acquisition of Research Medical Inc, a Salt Lake City-based medical device firm whose shareholders approved the transaction on March 14.

As previously announced, a big chunk of the purchase price for both Research Medical and Immuno will be allocated to in-process research and development, resulting in a non-cash charge of about $360 million to first-quarter earnings.
Baxter said the Research Medical acquisition will enable it to capitalize on opportunities in the evolving field of minimally invasive cardiac surgery.
Both acquisitions, said Chairman Vernon Loucks Jr in a statement, "support our key strategic initiatives of technological innovation and global expansion,".

Kraemer, meanwhile, said Baxter expects "to generate a minimum of $300 million in operational cash flow in 1997, excluding litigation expenses, after investing almost $1 billion in research and development and capital expenditures during the year."
Baxter, a medical products and services company, ended up 1/2 at 46-7/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.
